ON MARCH 23, the 115th birth anniversary of
Ram Manohar Lohia, Prime Minister Narendra
Modi remembered him as a “visionary leader,
fierce freedom fighter and an icon of social jus-
tice”. With the usual exception of Lohiaite so-
Cialist partieslike the Samajwadi Party and the
Rashtriya Janata Dal, the Opposition has made
little attempt & draw upon Lohia's political and
ideobgicallegacy. Hs egacy remains shrouded
in distorted memoriesofhis mercurial politics.
Lohia's most potent ideas — his reformulation of
the received socialistdoctrine and the accompa-
nying political and policy prescriptions — have
not travelled beyond a small and dwindling
band of Lohiaites. This is a tragedy, not just for
the INDIA bloc, butalso for India.
Thisisnotthe firsttime that Modiand other
BJP leaders have invoked Lohia. Many of his
Stancesand caichipnrases have been twisted by
BjPideologues to serve their ends, contradict-
ing Lohia's political positions. His attacks on
Jawaharlal Nehru are relished by BJP leaders,
and used to push agendas on which Lohia
would have actually agreed with the former
PM. His “anti-Congressism” has been used as
astick with which tobeat Congressand as afig
leaf by some ex-socialists to defend their al-
liance with the BJP. His slogan of “Banish
English” is used to support Hindi imposition,
and his staunch support for backward castes is

inates the Indian mind when it is in retreat.

forms, demands forjusticeand extemal in-
fluences. What is presented as Hindus vs
Muslims or other minorities is, at itscore,a

Hinduism. When the liberal streak domi-
nates Hinduism, India is on the ascent. The
rise ofilliberal or narrow Hinduism — asin
recent times — is associated with India's de-
cline asa nation and a civilisation.

limited tohis iwsefuness tocontemporary pol-
itics. Beyond the above, Lohia's enduring
legacy is that he provided the philosophical
foundations for India's own modemity. He of-
fered a rigorous critique of the Eurocentric as-
sumptions of Westem theories, including

its mythology ofour great past. While firmly
committed to social and economic egaltari-
anism, Lohia also laid the grounds for the pol-

the blueprint for anew form of radicalism. You
